items.title: Folium of Descartes
paragraphs: Interchanging x,y leaves the equation unchanged: symmetry is about y=x. The lowest-degree equation at the origin is xy=0, giving the two axes as nodal tangents. The only intercept on either coordinate axis is the origin.
On y=x, \(2x^3=3ax^2\), giving the origin and (3a/2,3a/2).
At (3a/2,3a/2), y′=−1, so the tangent is x+y=3a.
Substitute y=mx+c in the equation. The coefficient of x³ gives 1+m³=0, hence m=−1. The coefficient of x² then gives 3c+3a=0, so c=−a. The oblique asymptote is x+y+a=0.
PankusDesk completion for branch locations: the parametrisation \(x=3at/(1+t^3),y=3at^2/(1+t^3)\) shows a first-quadrant loop for t>0 and the two unbounded branches for t<0, separated by t=−1.
items.final_answer: A first-quadrant loop, node at the origin, symmetry about y=x, and asymptote x+y+a=0.
